item.content:encoded:
Arsenal and Manchester United are reportedly interested in signing Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi as both Premier League clubs look to add attacking reinforcements ahead of next summer’s transfer window.

According to a report from Football Insider, the two English giants are among several clubs monitoring the 22-year-old, who has emerged as one of Europe’s most exciting young goalscorers.

Nicolo Tresoldi attracts interest from Arsenal and Manchester United

The German-born Italian forward has enjoyed an outstanding campaign with Club Brugge, scoring 12 goals in 14 appearances across all competitions.

His Champions League performances have been particularly impressive, with Tresoldi currently sharing the competition’s top scorer position alongside established superstars Harry Kane and Erling Haaland.

The youngster has already shown he can deliver against elite opposition, scoring a hat-trick against Inter Milan in October. He has also found the net against Aston Villa, further strengthening his reputation among Europe’s leading clubs.

Arsenal could view Tresoldi as an exciting long-term investment as Mikel Arteta looks to maintain competition within his attacking department. The Gunners have already completed a successful transfer with Club Brugge, signing Christos Tzolis, and could look to repeat that business with another highly rated talent.

Manchester United are also interested in strengthening their forward line, and Tresoldi’s movement, finishing ability and potential could make him an attractive addition.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Club Brugge reluctant to sell Tresoldi

However, securing his signature will not be straightforward. Club Brugge have no intention of letting the striker leave during the January transfer window and are determined to keep him until the end of the season.

The Belgian club knows his performances have attracted considerable attention and could struggle to hold on to him next summer.

Tresoldi remains under contract until 2029, giving Brugge a strong negotiating position.

With Tottenham and Chelsea also monitoring his situation, Arsenal and Manchester United could face considerable competition. Both clubs may therefore need to prepare substantial offers if they want to win the race for his signature.

item.content:encoded:
Barcelona are reportedly interested in signing Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez as Hansi Flick looks to strengthen his defensive options ahead of the January transfer window.

According to an exclusive report from TEAMtalk, the Spanish champions have already made enquiries about the Argentina international, who has indicated that he is prepared to leave Old Trafford next summer.

Lisandro Martinez attracts Barcelona interest

The 28-year-old has experienced a difficult period at Manchester United, with injuries and inconsistent team performances raising questions about his long-term future at the club.

Despite those difficulties, Martinez remains highly regarded across Europe, and his ability to operate as a left-sided centre-back makes him an attractive option for Barcelona.

Flick wants to add an experienced defender to his squad, especially as the club looks to improve its options alongside Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin.

Barcelona have previously considered moves for Inter Milan’s Alessandro Bastoni, but securing his services could prove difficult. Martinez represents a potentially more attainable alternative, and the Catalan giants have already explored the conditions of a possible transfer.

The Argentine could also welcome a fresh challenge after telling United he wants to move on from the club.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Manchester United face decision over Martinez future

However, Barcelona will need to negotiate with Manchester United before completing a deal. Martinez’s current contract expires next summer, although United have an option to extend his stay by another 12 months.

Activating that clause would allow United to protect his transfer value and maintain greater control over his future.

The situation could become particularly interesting in January, with Barcelona keen to strengthen their defence during the winter window rather than wait until the summer.

Manchester United must now decide whether to retain Martinez or consider offers for a player who appears ready for a new challenge.

With Barcelona already making enquiries, a potential transfer could gather momentum in the coming months. The Spanish giants could offer the defender an opportunity to revive his career, while United may prefer to negotiate a sale rather than risk losing him without a transfer fee.

item.content:encoded:
Manchester United have reportedly suffered a setback in their pursuit of Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with the England international preparing to commit his future to the Elland Road club.

According to a BBC report, the 29-year-old has decided to sign a new contract with Leeds, despite attracting interest from Michael Carrick’s side ahead of the January transfer window.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin attracts Manchester United interest

The striker has enjoyed an impressive resurgence since joining Leeds from Everton in 2025, becoming a key figure in their attack.

Calvert-Lewin scored 14 goals in 35 Premier League appearances last season and has continued his impressive form this campaign, finding the net five times in his first 10 matches across competitions.

His performances have attracted attention from Manchester United, who are exploring the possibility of bringing in another centre-forward during the winter transfer window, according to the Athletic via TEAMtalk.

The Red Devils could benefit from signing an experienced Premier League striker, especially with Benjamin Sesko facing an extended spell on the sidelines due to a shin injury.

Calvert-Lewin’s physical presence, aerial ability and experience in English football could make him a useful addition to Carrick’s squad. However, United have now received disappointing news regarding his availability.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Leeds United set to secure new deal for Calvert-Lewin

According to BBC journalist Simon Stone, Calvert-Lewin is set to sign a new contract with Leeds, effectively ending Manchester United’s hopes of securing his services in January.

The development represents a significant boost for Daniel Farke, who considers the striker an important part of his plans.

Leeds are determined to retain their leading goalscorer and have moved quickly to protect his long-term future.

Manchester United will now have to explore alternative options as they continue their search for attacking reinforcements. Nicolo Tresoldi, Igor Matanovic and Jean-Philippe Mateta are among the forwards linked with the club.

With Sesko unavailable, finding another reliable goalscorer remains a priority for United, but Calvert-Lewin’s decision means they may need to look elsewhere.

item.content:encoded:
Liverpool are reportedly keeping tabs on Bayern Munich youngster Lennart Karl as Arne Slot considers potential attacking reinforcements ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

According to a report from CFBayernInsider, the Reds are among several Premier League clubs exploring a move for the highly rated German teenager, with Arsenal and Manchester United also monitoring his situation.

Lennart Karl attracts Liverpool interest

The 18-year-old has emerged as one of Germany’s most exciting young talents after enjoying an impressive breakthrough campaign at Bayern Munich. He registered nine goals and seven assists in 34 appearances last season, earning recognition at senior international level.

However, Karl has struggled to secure regular opportunities this season, with competition for attacking positions limiting his involvement under Vincent Kompany. The arrival of Ismael Saibari has made things more difficult for the youngster, potentially creating uncertainty about his long-term development in Munich.

Liverpool could benefit from adding another technically gifted attacking midfielder to their squad. Karl’s creativity, close control and ability to operate in multiple attacking positions would make him an exciting prospect for Slot.

Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, has also publicly criticised the teenager, suggesting he needs to remain humble and focus on his development. Nevertheless, Christian Falk believes the club’s senior decision-makers remain confident in his potential.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Liverpool face competition for Karl

According to Falk, representatives from Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United have already made enquiries to understand the situation.

Karl is reportedly valued at around €60 million, making a potential transfer financially achievable for the Premier League giants. However, Bayern are determined to retain him and have no immediate intention of sanctioning his departure.

The German international signed a contract running until 2029, meaning the Bundesliga champions remain in a strong negotiating position.

Liverpool could therefore face a difficult task if they decide to formalise their interest. Much will depend on Karl’s playing time and how his relationship with Bayern develops over the coming months.

With several Premier League clubs monitoring developments, his future could become an interesting transfer story heading into 2027.

item.content:encoded:
Manchester United are reportedly eyeing up a potential transfer move for Fulham defender Calvin Bassey amid their issues in that area of their squad.

Lisandro Martinez wants out of Old Trafford and this will likely lead the Red Devils to look to the transfer market for replacements, possibly including Como’s Jacobo Ramon.

Ramon has been linked with Man Utd and other top clubs by the Daily Mail, so there could also be some substance to TEAMtalk‘s report linking Bassey as another target for the club.

United will likely have other options on their radar, but Bassey looks tempting after his strong form for Fulham, as he’s proven he can be one of the most solid defensive players in the Premier League.

The 26-year-old is mostly a centre-back, but he could also provide an option for United at left-back if required, which could be worth thinking about as Luke Shaw comes towards the end of his contract.

Calvin Bassey on Manchester United’s radar

Bassey is on United’s radar, but they’re not the only club showing a growing interest in the Nigeria international.

TEAMtalk report that Newcastle, Everton, Inter Milan, Borussia Dortmund, and RB Leipzig are also keen on Bassey, so he won’t necessarily be heading to Manchester.

Bassey might well look at United’s current situation and question if they’d really be the best move for him anyway.

It’s been a dire season for MUFC and it could mean a managerial change is soon needed to turn the team’s fortunes around.

Having said that, Bassey would probably also still see the move as a step up from Fulham, who haven’t made a great start to the season either, currently sitting in 15th place in the table.

item.content:encoded:
Arsenal, Liverpool, and Manchester United have been mentioned as clubs to watch amid uncertainty over Lennart Karl’s Bayern Munich future.

Writing in his exclusive CF Bayern Insider column, Christian Falk provided some insight into Karl’s situation after public criticism from Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness.

The 18-year-old is a highly regarded talent who could have a big future at Bayern, but in his relatively short career so far he’s already rubbed the club up the wrong way a few times.

Karl previously made public claims about dreaming of joining Real Madrid in the future, and he’s now been criticised by Hoeness after a dip in form.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Falk, however, is not convinced this will necessarily have a big impact on Karl’s future, even if he is aware of some interest from the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, and Man Utd.

Lennart Karl transfer situation explained by Christian Falk

Responding to recent headlines involving Karl, Falk made it clear that Hoeness is not part of the everyday management of the club, who are happy with the German teenager.

Still, he also admitted some calls have been made and a deal could be possible for the right price.

“The latest Uli Hoeness statement on Lennart Karl was a typical one from the FC Bayern chief,” Falk wrote. “He’s made similar kinds of comments in the past about previous Bayern players.

“I remember when he spoke out against Bastian Schweinsteiger when there was a special case about his behaviour off the pitch (dying his hair bleach-blonde and having black nails).”

He added: “Uli likes to push people’s buttons or, as we say in Germany, walk on the cookie until the sugar falls out. It’s the same case with Lennart Karl. It’s worth pointing out that Hoeness, who is on the supervisory board, isn’t involved in the daily business of the club. Those who are involved in the daily business are very confident in Karl. They want to keep him.

“Of course, the Premier League is also reading what is being said in Germany. I heard that Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United saw that there is something going on around Lennart Karl.

“So calls have been made to ascertain what’s going on with the player and whether anyone’s not totally satisfied with the young German in Munich. He’s got a value of €60m [£50.1m], so it’s more than possible for Premier League clubs. It’s getting interesting. Until now, there haven’t been any talks over a new contract.”

item.content:encoded:
Arsenal, Manchester United, and Chelsea are reportedly all showing an interest in Como’s talented young centre-back Jacobo Ramon.

The 21-year-old has established himself as one of the top young defenders in Europe in recent times, forming a key part of this hugely impressive Como side.

Ramon has been on the radar of top Premier League clubs for some time, as previously revealed via the Daily Briefing, and there’s now been a further update.

It seems Arsenal, Man Utd, and Chelsea remain the main suitors for Ramon, though his situation is complicated by Real Madrid having a sell-on clause and buy-back clause, according to the Daily Mail.

The Spain Under-21 international’s market value is now likely to have risen to around €50m, according to Tuttomercatoweb.

What does the future hold for Jacobo Ramon?

Ramon, similarly to Nico Paz, started out at Real Madrid and has developed superbly since moving to Como.

Los Blancos will surely be tempted to try re-signing these players, even if their fine form will also have attracted strong interest from elsewhere.

Real Madrid look to have done well to insert both a buy-back clause and sell-on clause in Ramon’s deal with Como, putting them firmly in control of his future.

The Premier League could be tempting for him, though, with Arsenal a particularly exciting project right now, where defenders have really thrived under the management of Mikel Arteta.

Jacobo Ramon to replace Lisandro Martinez?

Ramon is also just the kind of young talent who’d appeal to Chelsea, but perhaps a move to United could make the most sense for him right now.

As revealed via today’s Daily Briefing exclusive, Lisandro Martinez could be on his way out of Old Trafford soon, and he’s on the radar of Como as a possible replacement for Ramon.

Perhaps MUFC could have some advantage in the race for Ramon if they could include Martinez in a deal for him this January.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Still, United are not in a good way right now and that might hurt them, whereas Arsenal look like title favourites and Chelsea at least look like a good club for young players to get the chance to play regularly and develop, even if things aren’t going entirely to plan on the pitch.

item.content:encoded:
Liverpool, Arsenal, and Manchester United are reportedly among the long list of clubs eyeing up exciting Galatasaray youngster Aleksey Batrakov.

The talented 21-year-old first caught the eye at former club Lokomotiv Moscow before joining Galatasaray this summer, and it seems Europe’s elite are all keeping a close eye on him.

With a £50m release clause in his contract, the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal, and Man Utd are mentioned as suitors for Batrakov, though they’re not alone.

According to TEAMtalk, Chelsea and Manchester City could be in the mix too, though there’s some suggestion that Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain could be viewed as more favourable options for him.

What next for Aleksey Batrakov?

Batrakov looks like a huge prospect, so it’s not too surprising that there’s already some uncertainty over his Galatasaray future, even though he only recently joined them.

The Russia international will want to choose his next club carefully, and TEAMtalk are claiming that he’s leaning towards Barca and PSG over Premier League clubs at the moment.

The ‘stature’ and ‘style of play’ of those two teams is said to be appealing to Batrakov, but it’s also important to note that Galatasaray are not keen to sell, according to the report.

We’ll have to see how this pans out, but for now it looks like this is just early interest and something unlikely to accelerate straight away.

item.content:encoded:
Manchester United are reportedly considering a surprise January move for Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as they look to strengthen their attacking options following Benjamin Sesko’s injury setback.

According to the Daily Mail, the Red Devils are exploring the possibility of signing the 29-year-old England international during the winter transfer window.

Manchester United interested in January move for Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Calvert-Lewin has enjoyed an impressive resurgence at Elland Road since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in the summer of 2025.

The striker scored 15 goals during his debut campaign and has continued his excellent form this season, registering five goals in ten appearances.

However, the report adds that signing him will not be straightforward as it will be a challenge to convince Leeds to part ways with their leading forward midway through the campaign, specially to Man United given their fierce historic rivalry

Benjamin Sesko injury could force Manchester United into January transfer market

United’s interest in Calvert-Lewin comes amid growing concerns over their attacking options.

Benjamin Sesko is expected to remain sidelined until at least January 2027 after suffering a setback with a persistent shin injury.

Fabrizio Romano recently reported, citing The Athletic, that Manchester United want the Slovenian striker to make a complete recovery before returning to competitive action.

The club are therefore unwilling to rush the 23-year-old back into the squad.

Sesko’s absence leaves manager Michael Carrick short of recognised centre-forward options.

United have struggled for consistency in the Premier League, with their recent 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth extending their winless run to eight matches across all competitions.

Carrick’s side currently sit 14th in the table, increasing the pressure on the club to improve its attacking performances.

While Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo can operate in advanced positions, Calvert-Lewin would offer a more traditional centre-forward presence.

Calvert-Lewin could be a fantastic stop gap signing for Man United

Calvert-Lewin’s Premier League experience makes him an intriguing option for Manchester United.

The England international has spent much of his senior career playing in the Premier League and has demonstrated his ability to score goals at the highest level.

His physical presence and aerial ability could be particularly useful for a United side that has struggled to establish a consistent attacking focal point.

Having revived his career at Leeds, the striker also appears to have regained the confidence that made him such an important player during his best years at Everton.

item.content:encoded:
Everton have been tipped to make a surprise January move for Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford, with former Toffees chief executive Keith Wyness claiming the possibility is being seriously discussed.

The 28-year-old has endured a difficult start to the 2026/27 campaign at Old Trafford, struggling for regular playing time under Michael Carrick.

Wyness believes a move to Everton could offer the England international an opportunity to rediscover his best form.

Keith Wyness claims Marcus Rashford to Everton move is being discussed

Speaking to Football Insider, the former Everton CEO suggested there is growing discussion surrounding a potential switch to the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Wyness believes Everton could emerge as an interesting destination for Rashford, particularly given the player’s previous success away from Manchester United.

The former Goodison Park chief pointed towards Rashford’s loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona as evidence that a change of environment could benefit the forward.

He said:

“This is definitely being talked about and quite strongly, and I think that could be an interesting solution. Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well.

“I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well.

“We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton.

“So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed. I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

Marcus Rashford yet to score for Manchester United this season

Rashford’s future has become an increasingly interesting talking point following his difficult start to the campaign.

The England international has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter under Carrick and is yet to open his goalscoring account in any competition this season.

His lack of minutes has made it difficult to build momentum, with United themselves enduring a disappointing run of results.

The Red Devils currently sit 14th in the Premier League table following their 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth.

With Carrick under mounting pressure and the club desperately searching for attacking solutions, Rashford’s position in the squad remains uncertain.

A January exit could potentially provide the forward with an opportunity to secure more consistent playing time.

For Everton, meanwhile, signing a player of Rashford’s experience would represent a significant statement of intent.
